title: PostgreSQL internals, Part 6: isolation levels and locking
tldr: How PostgreSQL keeps concurrent transactions from corrupting each other, and what goes wrong when they wait: lost updates, Read Committed's per-statement snapshots and WHERE re-checks, Repeatable Read and serialization failures, Serializable and write skew, the eight table lock modes, row locks and SELECT FOR UPDATE, SKIP LOCKED job queues, advisory locks, the retry loop for 40001 and 40P01, deadlocks and lock order, the migration lock queue and lock_timeout, idle transactions, PgBouncer pitfalls, choosing a strategy, and an interview drill. The final part of the series.
